:::{#exm-proof-by-contrapositive}
#### If $x^2 + 3x < 0$, then $x < 0$

Claim: for every [real number](number-systems.qmd#def-real-numbers) $x$,
if $x^2 + 3x < 0$, then $x < 0$.

A [direct proof](#def-direct-proof) would have to start from the [inequality](#def-inequality) $x^2 + 3x < 0$,
which says little about $x$ on its own.
The contrapositive (@def-contrapositive) is
"if $x \ge 0$, then $x^2 + 3x \ge 0$",
and its assumption is easier to use.

Suppose $x \ge 0$.
Then $x^2 = x \cd x \ge 0$,
because a product of two nonnegative numbers is nonnegative, <!-- check-term-links: allow -->
and $3x \ge 0$,
because $3 > 0$ and $x \ge 0$.
So

$$
\ba
x^2 + 3x
&\ge 0 + 0
&& \text{(add the inequalities } x^2 \ge 0 \text{ and } 3x \ge 0 \text{)}
\\&= 0.
&& \text{(arithmetic)}
\ea
$$

That proves the contrapositive,
so by @thm-contrapositive the claim holds.
For example, $x = -1$ gives $x^2 + 3x = 1 - 3 = -2 < 0$, and indeed $x < 0$.

:::
